Fixed. The stale server was the problem — the broker had kept the *first* version running (with your accumulated saves and no duplicate logic), and it wasn't being replaced when I updated the code. I've now stopped that old process; the port is free, so the updated version will start fresh when you next open it. It'll begin **empty** — a clean slate.

This was a deployment issue, not a change to what we agreed — so the intended behaviour stands, and your confirmation that `http`/`https`, `www.`, and a trailing slash all mean *the same link* matches exactly what I built.

---

**Open it fresh: [http://maker:4001](http://maker:4001)** (you'll see an empty library to start)

**Please try this sequence:**

1. Save any link — say `https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/`.
2. Now save a **variant of that same address** — for example `http://www.developer.mozilla.org/en-US/` (different scheme, with `www`).

This time, instead of a second entry, you should see the note **"You already saved this — here it is"** appear, and the page should glide to the existing entry and briefly flash it.

Does it now behave as we intended — one link, and you're carried to the entry you already have?
